correctness.rationale: With the stated Fourier convention, the inverse transform of the principal-value multiplier \(1/\xi\) is \((i/2)\operatorname{sign}x\); mean zero therefore turns \(|D|^{-1}\operatorname{sign}(D)f\) into \(iF\). The Hermitian pairing is twice the signed area of the closed primitive curve, and the sharp signed isoperimetric inequality gives \(2|\mathcal A(F)|\le \|f\|_1^2/(2\pi)\), with circles as the equality cases. The argument also lets a finite regularized difference transfer finiteness from one half-frequency energy to the other. A local proof typo was detected in RESULT.md: it prints a minus sign in the displayed formula for \(\operatorname{Im}(F'\overline F)\); direct multiplication gives the positive area integrand. The immediately following pairing and final identity use the correct sign, so the theorem and sharp constant are unchanged. This is treated as a non-substantive proof-line defect, not a false final claim.
